passages.text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied: “Can a man be of use to God? Can even a wise man benefit Him?
passages.sermon:
Eliphaz was a man from Teman.
Eliphaz spoke.
Eliphaz replied to Job.
Eliphaz asked a question.
Can a man help God?
Can a person be useful to God?
Can a wise man give any benefit to God?
Can a person with understanding profit God?
passages.original: וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ הַלְאֵ֥ל יִסְכָּן־ גָּ֑בֶר כִּֽי־ יִסְכֹּ֖ן עָלֵ֣ימוֹ מַשְׂכִּֽיל׃

passages.text: Does it delight the Almighty that you are righteous? Does He profit if your ways are blameless?
passages.sermon:
Eliphaz the Temanite spoke to Job.
Eliphaz asked about God.
God is the Almighty.
Eliphaz asked if God finds joy when a person is righteous.
Eliphaz asked if God gains anything when a person’s ways are blameless.
passages.original: הַחֵ֣פֶץ לְ֭שַׁדַּי כִּ֣י תִצְדָּ֑ק וְאִם־ בֶּ֝֗צַע כִּֽי־ תַתֵּ֥ם דְּרָכֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Is it for your reverence that He rebukes you and enters into judgment against you?
passages.sermon:
Eliphaz the Temanite spoke to Job.
Eliphaz asked Job a question.
God is the judge.
God rebukes people.
God enters into judgment with people.
Eliphaz asked if God rebuked Job because Job feared God.
Eliphaz asked if God judged Job because of Job’s reverence.
passages.original: הֲֽ֭מִיִּרְאָ֣תְךָ יֹכִיחֶ֑ךָ יָב֥וֹא עִ֝מְּךָ֗ בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: Is not your wickedness great? Are not your iniquities endless?
passages.sermon: Your wickedness is very great.\r\nYour iniquities have no end.
passages.original: הֲלֹ֣א רָעָֽתְךָ֣ רַבָּ֑ה וְאֵֽין־ קֵ֝֗ץ לַעֲוֺנֹתֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: For you needlessly demanded security from your brothers and deprived the naked of their clothing.
passages.sermon: You demanded security from your brothers for no reason.\r\nYou took clothing from people who were naked.\r\nYou left them without what they needed.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תַחְבֹּ֣ל אַחֶ֣יךָ חִנָּ֑ם וּבִגְדֵ֖י עֲרוּמִּ֣ים תַּפְשִֽׁיט׃

passages.text: You gave no water to the weary and withheld food from the famished, while the land belonged to a mighty man, and a man of honor lived on it.
passages.sermon:
You did not give water to people who were tired.
You kept food from people who were hungry.
A strong man owned the land.
A respected man lived there.
passages.original: לֹא־ מַ֭יִם עָיֵ֣ף תַּשְׁקֶ֑ה וּ֝מֵרָעֵ֗ב תִּֽמְנַֽע־ לָֽחֶם׃ וְאִ֣ישׁ זְ֭רוֹעַ ל֣וֹ הָאָ֑רֶץ וּנְשׂ֥וּא פָ֝נִ֗ים יֵ֣שֶׁב בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: You sent widows away empty-handed, and the strength of the fatherless was crushed.
passages.sermon:
You sent widows away with nothing.
You gave them no help.
You crushed the strength of orphans.
You harmed those who had no father to protect them.
passages.original: אַ֭לְמָנוֹת שִׁלַּ֣חְתָּ רֵיקָ֑ם וּזְרֹע֖וֹת יְתֹמִ֣ים יְדֻכָּֽא׃

passages.text: Therefore snares surround you, and sudden peril terrifies you; it is so dark you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you.
passages.sermon:
You acted with injustice and withheld help from those in need.
Because of this, traps now surround you.
Sudden fear terrifies you.
Darkness is so great that you cannot see.
A flood of water covers you.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֭ן סְבִיבוֹתֶ֣יךָ פַחִ֑ים וִֽ֝יבַהֶלְךָ פַּ֣חַד פִּתְאֹֽם׃ אוֹ־ חֹ֥שֶׁךְ לֹֽא־ תִרְאֶ֑ה וְֽשִׁפְעַת־ מַ֥יִם תְּכַסֶּֽךָּ׃

passages.text: Is not God as high as the heavens? Look at the highest stars, how lofty they are!
passages.sermon:
God is very high.
God is higher than the heavens.
The stars are very high in the sky.
The highest stars are lofty.
God is even higher than the highest stars.
passages.original: הֲ‍ֽלֹא־ אֱ֭לוֹהַּ גֹּ֣בַהּ שָׁמָ֑יִם וּרְאֵ֤ה רֹ֖אשׁ כּוֹכָבִ֣ים כִּי־ רָֽמּוּ׃

passages.text: Yet you say: ‘What does God know? Does He judge through thick darkness?
passages.sermon:
You say these words to God.
You ask, “What does God know?”
You question God’s knowledge.
You ask, “Can God judge through thick darkness?”
You wonder if darkness hides things from God.
You doubt that God can see and judge everything.
passages.original: וְֽ֭אָמַרְתָּ מַה־ יָּ֣דַֽע אֵ֑ל הַבְעַ֖ד עֲרָפֶ֣ל יִשְׁפּֽוֹט׃

passages.text: Thick clouds veil Him so He does not see us as He traverses the vault of heaven.’
passages.sermon:
God is the subject.
Thick clouds hide God.
God does not see us.
God walks on the circle of the sky.
passages.original: עָבִ֣ים סֵֽתֶר־ ל֭וֹ וְלֹ֣א יִרְאֶ֑ה וְח֥וּג שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם יִתְהַלָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Will you stay on the ancient path that wicked men have trod?
passages.sermon:
You face a choice.
You can follow a path.
This path is very old.
Wicked men walked on this path before.
Will you keep walking on this ancient path?
Wicked people chose this way in the past.
passages.original: הַאֹ֣רַח עוֹלָ֣ם תִּשְׁמֹ֑ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר דָּרְכ֣וּ מְתֵי־ אָֽוֶן׃

passages.text: They were snatched away before their time, and their foundations were swept away by a flood.
passages.sermon:
Wicked men lived on the ancient path.
God judged these wicked men.
God took them away suddenly.
They died before their time.
A flood destroyed their foundations.
Their lives and security ended quickly.
passages.original: אֲשֶֽׁר־ קֻמְּט֥וּ וְלֹא־ עֵ֑ת נָ֝הָ֗ר יוּצַ֥ק יְסוֹדָֽם׃

passages.text: They said to God, ‘Depart from us. What can the Almighty do to us?’
passages.sermon: Wicked men spoke to God.\r\nThey told God, "Leave us."\r\nThey asked, "What can the Almighty do to us?"
passages.original: הָאֹמְרִ֣ים לָ֭אֵל ס֣וּר מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וּמַה־ יִּפְעַ֖ל שַׁדַּ֣י לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: But it was He who filled their houses with good things; so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.
passages.sermon: God filled their houses with good things.\r\nI stay far from the advice of wicked people.
passages.original: וְה֤וּא מִלֵּ֣א בָתֵּיהֶ֣ם ט֑וֹב וַעֲצַ֥ת רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים רָ֣חֲקָה מֶֽנִּי׃

passages.text: The righteous see it and are glad; the innocent mock them: ‘Surely our foes are destroyed, and fire has consumed their excess.’
passages.sermon:
The righteous see what happened.
The righteous feel glad.
The innocent see it too.
The innocent mock those people.
They say, "Our enemies are gone."
They say, "Fire has destroyed what they had left."
passages.original: יִרְא֣וּ צַדִּיקִ֣ים וְיִשְׂמָ֑חוּ וְ֝נָקִ֗י יִלְעַג־ לָֽמוֹ׃ אִם־ לֹ֣א נִכְחַ֣ד קִימָ֑נוּ וְ֝יִתְרָ֗ם אָ֣כְלָה אֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: Reconcile now and be at peace with Him; thereby good will come to you.
passages.sermon:
God is the Almighty.
You must reconcile with Him now.
You must make peace with Him.
If you do this, good will come to you.
passages.original: הַסְכֶּן־ נָ֣א עִמּ֑וֹ וּשְׁלם בָּ֝הֶ֗ם תְּֽבוֹאַתְךָ֥ טוֹבָֽה׃

passages.text: Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart.
passages.sermon:
God speaks.
God gives instruction.
Listen to God’s instruction.
Take God’s words into your heart.
Remember what God says.
Keep His words inside you.
passages.original: קַח־ נָ֣א מִפִּ֣יו תּוֹרָ֑ה וְשִׂ֥ים אֲ֝מָרָ֗יו בִּלְבָבֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored. If you remove injustice from your tents and consign your gold to the dust and the gold of Ophir to the stones of the ravines, then the Almighty will be your gold and the finest silver for you.
passages.sermon:
The Almighty is God.
If you return to the Almighty, He will restore you.
Remove injustice from your home.
Throw your gold onto the dust.
Throw the gold of Ophir onto the stones in the ravines.
Then the Almighty will be your treasure.
The Almighty will be your finest silver.
passages.original: אִם־ תָּשׁ֣וּב עַד־ שַׁ֭דַּי תִּבָּנֶ֑ה תַּרְחִ֥יק עַ֝וְלָ֗ה מֵאָהֳלֶֽךָ׃ וְשִׁית־ עַל־ עָפָ֥ר בָּ֑צֶר וּבְצ֖וּר נְחָלִ֣ים אוֹפִֽיר׃ וְהָיָ֣ה שַׁדַּ֣י בְּצָרֶ֑יךָ וְכֶ֖סֶף תּוֹעָפ֣וֹת לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Surely then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
passages.sermon: The Almighty is God.\r\nYou will delight in the Almighty.\r\nYou will lift up your face to God.
passages.original: כִּי־ אָ֭ז עַל־ שַׁדַּ֣י תִּתְעַנָּ֑ג וְתִשָּׂ֖א אֶל־ אֱל֣וֹהַּ פָּנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: You will pray to Him, and He will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
passages.sermon: You will pray to God.\r\nGod will hear you.\r\nYou will fulfill your vows.
passages.original: תַּעְתִּ֣יר אֵ֭לָיו וְיִשְׁמָעֶ֑ךָּ וּנְדָרֶ֥יךָ תְשַׁלֵּֽם׃

passages.text: Your decisions will be carried out, and light will shine on your ways.
passages.sermon:
God is the Almighty.
God listens to those who delight in Him.
You will make a decision.
Your decision will happen.
Light will shine on your path.
Your way will be clear.
passages.original: וְֽתִגְזַר־ א֭וֹמֶר וְיָ֣קָם לָ֑ךְ וְעַל־ דְּ֝רָכֶ֗יךָ נָ֣גַֽהּ אֽוֹר׃

passages.text: When men are brought low and you say, ‘Lift them up!’ then He will save the lowly.
passages.sermon:
God sees people who are humble.
Some people are brought low.
You say to them, “Be lifted up.”
God saves those who are humble.
God helps people who are lowly.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִ֭שְׁפִּילוּ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר גֵּוָ֑ה וְשַׁ֖ח עֵינַ֣יִם יוֹשִֽׁעַ׃

passages.text: He will deliver even one who is not innocent, rescuing him through the cleanness of your hands.”
passages.sermon:
God acts with power and mercy.
God can deliver a person who is not innocent.
God rescues that person because your hands are clean.
Your righteousness brings rescue for others.
passages.original: יְֽמַלֵּ֥ט אִֽי־ נָקִ֑י וְ֝נִמְלַ֗ט בְּבֹ֣ר כַּפֶּֽיךָ׃פ
